caption: The drawing depicts a double wooden door set within a stone archway. The doors are rectangular and are shown with wooden panels in a natural brown color, and are mounted with metal hinges and fixtures at the top and bottom corners. The arch above the door is composed of large, stone blocks outlined with blue-gray lines, radiating outward from the center in a semicircular shape. At the base of the arch, there is a horizontal band decorated with a geometric pattern in blue, white, gold, and red, followed by a band of plain white. Below this, the wall is rendered in a reddish-brown color with a marbled texture. The ground in front of the door is drawn as red-brown tiles arranged in a grid. The background is off-white and blank except for the doorway structure. There is a small, cursive inscription in black at the bottom right corner, including a name and the year “1936.”
title: Restoration Drawing
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
